Subject: StrataAI — tranche windowing & vendor cadence for dedicated pool

Hi Samantha / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I sketched a tranche/window approach to get StrataAI onto a dedicated pool without forcing a single long-tail hardware commitment up front. This aims to balance your cost predictability with OEM lead times and customs/port variability.

High-level proposal (draft):
- Tranche 1 (onramp): 6 weeks from PO — 32 H-class GPUs equivalent reserved; deliveries staged across 2 shipments to shorten customs exposure.
- Tranche 2 (scale): +96 GPUs targeted in week 7–12 (staged over 3 shipments).
- Tranche 3 (steady state): remaining capacity ramped month 4+ as manufacturing windows clear.

Bridging/backfill options:
- Short-term cloud bridge (Nebula) for first 6–8 weeks to absorb request spikes and keep latency SLOs intact.
- Prefix/KV caching tweaks to reduce immediate token spend while pools warm up.

Commercial asks / vendor coordination:
- Can Vertex confirm lead times for the H-class SKU (best case / typical / worst case) and whether they can commit a partial hold for a 15% deposit or escrow?
- Can Nebula commit to a burst pool rate card and how quickly they can spin up 32 nodes?

Attached: redwood_tranche_estimate_v1.xlsx (rough cost/schedule matrix).

Next steps I propose:
1) Vertex to provide a dated availability calendar and any conditional pricing for tranches.
2) Redwood to issue a draft PO cadence and short-form terms for Strata to review.
3) If agree, we route the tranche schedule to legal/procurement and lock a first shipment window.

Samantha — can you confirm Strata's appetite for a staged deposit vs. a single upfront commit? If there are internal procurement constraints (invoice cadence, net terms), note them here so we can align with our finance team.

Thanks,

— Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Thanks Stephanie — this looks promising. A few quick clarifications before we push to legal/procurement: 

1) Tranche sizing: we prefer three clearer delivery points (onramp, mid-scale, steady state). Can you split the second tranche into two smaller shipments (we're trying to avoid a single large import event)?
2) Deposit vs escrow: Strata's procurement is okay with a staged deposit (max 20%) if we get firm delivery windows attached to each tranche.
3) Invoice cadence: Strata requires net-45 for hardware POs — is Redwood able to accept net-45 on the hardware portion while charging monthly for hosted bridge credits?

I've attached our intake calendar (vertex_oem_availability.ics) showing blackout dates for our internal release cycles — avoid those weeks if possible. We'll loop procurement (procurement@strataai.com) after we have a draft PO cadence.

If Vertex can reply with the SKU lead-time buckets (best / normal / worst) and any required minimum tranche size, we can quickly convert this into a PO.

Samantha Lee

Nice summary — adding some concrete numbers/recommendations from the capacity side.

Quick answers / recommendations:
- Break Tranche 2 into 2 shipments: 48 GPUs at week 8 and 48 GPUs at week 10 (keeps individual import >$50k line items manageable).
- Tranche A (onramp): 32 GPUs (equivalent to 8 nodes sized for Strata's perf target). We can have the Nebula bridge up in ~72 hours for 32 nodes; billing for bridge is monthly.
- Lead-time buckets for Vertex H-class: Best: 4–6 weeks (slot already promised to enterprise customers), Typical: 8–12 weeks, Worst: 14–20+ weeks (manufacturing/port risk). We do see order clustering push to the right in Q4.
- Deposit: recommend a 15% staged deposit tied to ship windows (15% on PO, 10% on shipment 2) to avoid holding excess inventory on our balance sheet.

Operational notes:
- Customs / import: recommend soft-staggering shipments by 7–10 days to smooth freight lanes.
- If Vertex needs an initial confirmed ship-window to hold production capacity, we should provide a short-term LOI (non-binding) to secure a slot — Redwood can accept the LOI + 15% deposit model.

I'll mark this low-risk to the broader fleet plan provided we secure cloud bridge credits for weeks 1–8.
